criterion: M3 dated addition 6 (materials), second stage, by the author's decision of 2026-10-10: "keep engine versions, and improve them." The 8-harmonic iridescence and the symmetric clearcoat and transmission weights stay the default; the specification's forms stay behind Material::specExact only as a comparison control. This file sets bounds on where the engine's forms still err, against references closer to the physics than the existing ones.
written: 2026-10-10, after exploration probes (recorded below as exploration, not results) and before any change to the material model

exploration.iridescence: Against an exact polarized Airy reference (dielectric base, real indices, s and p averaged, CIE 1931 by the Wyman-Sloan-Shirley fit, white-balanced), the fast path errs by up to 0.16 to 0.26 per channel at cos 0.1 to 0.3, and by 0.02 to 0.03 at normal incidence. The existing spectral reference shares the fast path's Schlick interfaces, so it agrees with the fast path to 0.03 and misses this.
exploration.clearcoat: A white metal (isotropic or anisotropic) under a clear coat loses up to 23% of its energy with the default coat (0.13 with the specification's form): light the coat reflects back down is never returned. The worst case is at grazing view under a smooth coat.
exploration.volume: Beer-Lambert attenuation is applied as exp(-thickness / distance * ln c) for every direction; the path through the medium is thickness / |cos theta_t|, so oblique and rough transmission is attenuated too little.

iridescence_exact.what: the iridescent Fresnel against a float64 exact reference: polarized Airy summation of a film on a dielectric base (indices 1.33, 1.5 and 2.0), film ior 1.2 to 2.0 by 0.2, thickness 100 to 1000 nm by 50, cos theta 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 and 1, 380 to 780 nm by 1 nm, the same colour matching fit, white-balanced so a constant spectrum stays grey
iridescence_exact.control: the present fast path (Schlick interfaces) and the specification's two-harmonic form must both fail it

clearcoat_energy.what: white metal, anisotropy 0, 0.3, 0.6 and 1.0, base roughness 0.2, 0.6 and 1.0, under clearcoat 0.5 and 1 with coat roughness 0.05, 0.3 and 1.0, view cosine 0.05, 0.2, 0.5 and 1, azimuth 0, 45 and 90 degrees from the anisotropy direction, albedo by the test_pbr_energy quadrature
clearcoat_energy.control: the specification's coat (specExact) must fail it

volume_path_length.what: energy transmitted into a volume and carried to the depth of its thickness: the rough dielectric interface's transmission (ior 1.5, roughness 0.05, 0.25, 0.5 and 1, view cosine 0.1 to 1 by 0.1) with Beer-Lambert attenuation along each refracted direction's own path, thickness / |cos theta_t|, integrated by quadrature over the refracted directions (the reference); attenuation colour 0.5 at distances giving thickness / distance = 0.25, 1 and 2
volume_path_length.bound: |model - reference| <= 5e-3 absolute, per channel, at every point
volume_path_length.control: attenuation applied without the path-length term (the present model) must fail it

no_regression.what: test_pbr_energy --full, test_pbr_reciprocity and the GPU material parity on WARP and SwiftShader after the changes

not_covered_yet: Thin-walled transmission against a path-traced thin slab (two rough interfaces with internal bounces), and iridescence on metal bases against complex indices. Both are named here so they are not forgotten; each gets bounds before its own first run.
does_not_prove: That the forms match other renderers or the Khronos sample viewer; perceptual differences; anything about textures or normal maps.

method_note_1_2026_10_11.written: 2026-10-11, before the code below and its first run; the clearcoat_energy bound and its control are unchanged
method_note_1_2026_10_11.table_axis: The split-albedo tables A and B move from a theta axis to u = sqrt(mu), 128 columns, as the sheen table did. Run clearcoat-4 traced a 0.4% shortfall of E at view cosine 0.02 to the theta grid's coarseness at grazing. The means Aavg and Bavg are recomputed from the new tables. The anisotropic and dominant-direction tables keep their axes.
method_note_1_2026_10_11.compensation: The coat's weighting of the base, (1 - c E_c(mu_o))(1 - c E_c(mu_i)), stays. Light the coat reflects back down is returned by a reciprocal lobe added to the smooth class: f = D(mu_o) D(mu_i) / (pi Dbar), per channel, with D(mu) = c (1 - c E_c(mu)) Q(mu) and Dbar = 2 * integral of D(mu) mu dmu. Q(mu) is the base's reflectance weighted by the coat's albedo at the reflected direction: the integral of f_base(o, i) E_c(mu_i) cos over i. For a base of albedo E_b the layered albedo is then c E_c + (1 - c E_c) E_b, which is 1 for a white base and at most 1 otherwise.
method_note_1_2026_10_11.how_Q_is_read: E_c(mu_i) is represented by its values at 9 nodes on u = sqrt(mu) with piecewise-linear hats in u. New tables hold the white isotropic GGX lobe's energy in each hat, split by Schlick like A and B (32 view columns on u x 32 roughness rows x 9 hats x 2), and the hats' cosine moments against 1, A and B (32 roughness rows x 9). Q's specular part is read from the first, the multiple-scattering and diffuse parts from the second. The averages in Dbar come from the same tables (hat-by-hat products). An anisotropic base reads the isotropic tables at alpha = sqrt(alpha_x alpha_y); if the anisotropic points fail with that, the run is recorded and an anisotropic table is the next attempt.
method_note_1_2026_10_11.gpu: pbr.wgsl gets the same lobe and tables; the GPU material parity bound is unchanged.
method_note_1_2026_10_11.image_lighting: iblResponse adds D(mu_o) to the irradiance weight, which is the lobe's response to a uniform environment.
method_note_1_2026_10_11.not_covered: Sheen between coat and base, iridescence and transmission do not enter Q; the bound tests a white metal base only. Conservation (test_pbr_energy, albedo at most 1 + 1e-3 for every family) still applies to every family.

method_note_2_2026_10_11.written: 2026-10-11, after runs clearcoat-5 and clearcoat-6 (recorded in evidence/m3-materials2-runs.json) and before the change below runs
method_note_2_2026_10_11.finding: With the compensation lobe and projected hat coefficients, every isotropic point passes (albedo 0.9948 to 1.0001). The anisotropic points exceed 1 + 1e-3 by up to 3.1e-3. The same white anisotropic metal without a coat already reaches 1.0033: the coat passes the base's own furnace error through. A quadrature probe puts that error in the anisotropic split-albedo table A4 + B4 itself: -0.003 at normal view for anisotropy 0.6 (linear interpolation in k of a quantity that depends on k^2) and +0.018 at view cosine 0.05 across the anisotropy direction (the theta axis is coarse at grazing).
method_note_2_2026_10_11.change: The anisotropic tables (A4, B4 and the hat tables HA4, HB4 on the same grid) change two axes: view u = sqrt(mu) in place of theta, and anisotropy k^2 in place of k. Grid sizes, sample counts and every bound are unchanged. This departs from method note 1, which kept the anisotropic axes; recorded here before the run.
method_note_2_2026_10_11.bounds: Unchanged: clearcoat_energy |albedo - 1| <= 2e-2 and albedo <= 1 + 1e-3; the anisotropic furnace in test_pbr_energy keeps its 2e-2.

method_note_3_2026_10_11.written: 2026-10-11, after run clearcoat-7 and before the change below runs
method_note_3_2026_10_11.finding: After note 2 every point over 1 + 1e-3 (26 of 864, worst 1.00265) sits where the same base without a coat is already over it (worst 1.00269). The coat compensation adds nothing there. The base's excess is the A4 + B4 table: at grid nodes it reads about 5e-4 to 1.4e-3 low or high (1,024 samples), and between azimuth nodes up to 2.9e-3 low (a concave function of the azimuth read linearly).
method_note_3_2026_10_11.change: The azimuth axis of the anisotropic tables becomes v = sin^2(phi) (8 nodes), since the lobe depends on the azimuth through cos^2 and sin^2. Sample counts unchanged.
method_note_3_2026_10_11.if_it_still_fails: The excess part of clearcoat_energy stays an open failure, recorded with the uncoated base's own figure beside it; the next step would be more samples per anisotropic table entry, which costs table build time in every test.
